q: Does refrigerant lost while installing new ACs or chillers count in our Scope 1?
title: Refrigerant lost during new installations
short: Yes, if your own team does the charging, though it is usually small. IPCC 2006 puts installation losses at 0.2% to 1% of the charge for ACs and chillers, and 0.5% to 3% for commercial and industrial refrigeration. Measure it as gas bought for the new units minus their rated charge.
audience: Facility and EHS managers adding ACs, chillers or cold rooms

p: Installation loss (kg) = refrigerant bought or used for the new equipment minus the full rated charge of that equipment. Multiply by the gas's GWP from one IPCC report and add it to Scope 1 for the year. The first charge itself is not an emission; only what escapes is.

sections.h: IPCC defaults when you have no figures
ul: Residential and commercial AC, including heat pumps: 0.2% to 1% of the charge.
Stand-alone commercial units and medium or large commercial refrigeration: 0.5% to 3%.
Industrial refrigeration, including food processing and cold storage: 0.5% to 3%.
Transport refrigeration and domestic refrigerators: 0.2% to 1%. Vehicle AC: 0.2% to 0.5%.
The lower end reflects developed countries and the upper end developing countries, so justify the point you pick.
Your technicians charge from your cylinders: yours, in Scope 1.
A contractor charges from its own cylinders and hands over a working system: the loss is the contractor's.
Units that arrive pre-charged from the factory carry little loss at your site; any extra gas added for long pipe runs is charging you do.

example.title: Worked example: an office fit-out and a chiller
lines: 40 split ACs on R-32, 1.2 kg charge each (illustrative): 48 kg in total
At 1% installation loss: 0.48 kg x 771 (AR6) = 370 kg CO2e
One 400 kg R-134a chiller at 1%: 4 kg x 1,530 (AR6) = 6.1 t CO2e

senseible: Senseible records refrigerant top-up and gas purchase invoices as Scope 1 lines with the gas and kilograms shown on the bill, where the invoice prints them. Mark first-charge purchases so they are not read as leakage.
